defects.what: City field affordance is nearly invisible in dark mode: the pill fill is a very dark grey sitting on a near-black background with no visible border, so it does not read as a tappable selector — it looks like a dead strip of empty space.
defects.where: City pill above the 'Get started' CTA

defects.what: 'Skip' link is small mid-grey text on black; estimated contrast ~3.5–4:1 (likely below AA 4.5:1) and its tap area appears to be only the text line, well under a 44px target height.
Body caption text under the headline is rendered in a grey (~#8A8A8A on black, roughly 4–4.5:1) — borderline against AA 4.5:1 for the primary explanatory copy the patient must read.

measured_notes: Headline 'Turn confirmed': large white bold text on black, contrast ~19:1, reads first — hierarchy law satisfied.
CTA pill: white fill with dark 'Get started' label, contrast ~18:1; pill height ~56px, meets 44px target; spans full 16px gutters.

City pill: fill estimated ~#242422 on ~#000 background — pill-vs-canvas contrast ~1.5:1, no hairline border visible; internal label grey ~#9A9A9A on #242422 ≈ 4.5:1 but the control itself fails the affordance test.
No truncation/ellipsis observed; all copy fully visible.
Page dots: 3 indicators, active dot is white pill — acceptable; screen gutter spacing looks consistent ~16px.
No teal accent used on this surface except in the illustration; no selected/live state present — consistent with restraint law.
non_blocking_notes: Illustration uses a dark card with white hairline border — the only bordered element on screen, which makes the city pill's borderlessness more conspicuous by comparison; consider matching hairline treatment.
Teal squiggle accent is decorative; fine under restraint rules but slightly disconnected from any functional teal usage.
Consider a subtle border or #F4F4F2-outline on the city pill and bumping 'Skip' to a lighter grey (#B0B0B0+) with a padded 44px hit area.
one_line: Dark-mode slide fails on the invisible city-selector affordance and an under-contrast, undersized Skip link; headline and CTA are otherwise exemplary.
